1.web: Dead flies cause the oil of the perfumer to produce an evil odor; so does a little folly outweigh wisdom and honor.
1.asv: Dead flies cause the oil of the perfumer to send forth an evil odor; so doth a little folly outweigh wisdom and honor.

2.web: A wise man’s heart is at his right hand, but a fool’s heart at his left.
2.asv: A wise man’s heart is at his right hand; but a fool’s heart at his left.

3.web: Yes also, when the fool walks by the way, his understanding fails him, and he says to everyone that he is a fool.
3.asv: Yea also, when the fool walketh by the way, his understanding faileth him, and he saith to every one that he is a fool.

4.web: If the spirit of the ruler rises up against you, don’t leave your place; for gentleness lays great offenses to rest.
4.asv: If the spirit of the ruler rise up against thee, leave not thy place; for gentleness allayeth great offences.

5.web: There is an evil which I have seen under the sun, the sort of error which proceeds from the ruler.
5.asv: There is an evil which I have seen under the sun, as it were an error which proceedeth from the ruler:

6.web: Folly is set in great dignity, and the rich sit in a low place.
6.asv: folly is set in great dignity, and the rich sit in a low place.

7.web: I have seen servants on horses, and princes walking like servants on the earth.
7.asv: I have seen servants upon horses, and princes walking like servants upon the earth.

8.web: He who digs a pit may fall into it; and whoever breaks through a wall may be bitten by a snake.
8.asv: He that diggeth a pit shall fall into it; and whoso breaketh through a wall, a serpent shall bite him.

9.web: Whoever carves out stones may be injured by them. Whoever splits wood may be endangered thereby.
9.asv: Whoso heweth out stones shall be hurt therewith; and he that cleaveth wood is endangered thereby.

10.web: If the ax is blunt, and one doesn’t sharpen the edge, then he must use more strength; but skill brings success.
10.asv: If the iron be blunt, and one do not whet the edge, then must he put to more strength: but wisdom is profitable to direct.

11.web: If the snake bites before it is charmed, then is there no profit for the charmer’s tongue.
11.asv: If the serpent bite before it is charmed, then is there no advantage in the charmer.

12.web: The words of a wise man’s mouth are gracious; but a fool is swallowed by his own lips.
12.asv: The words of a wise man’s mouth are gracious; but the lips of a fool will swallow up himself.

13.web: The beginning of the words of his mouth is foolishness; and the end of his talk is mischievous madness.
13.asv: The beginning of the words of his mouth is foolishness; and the end of his talk is mischievous madness.

14.web: A fool also multiplies words. Man doesn’t know what will be; and that which will be after him, who can tell him?
14.asv: A fool also multiplieth words: yet man knoweth not what shall be; and that which shall be after him, who can tell him?

15.web: The labor of fools wearies every one of them; for he doesn’t know how to go to the city.
15.asv: The labor of fools wearieth every one of them; for he knoweth not how to go to the city.

16.web: Woe to you, land, when your king is a child, and your princes eat in the morning!
16.asv: Woe to thee, O land, when thy king is a child, and thy princes eat in the morning!

17.web: Happy are you, land, when your king is the son of nobles, and your princes eat in due season, for strength, and not for drunkenness!
17.asv: Happy art thou, O land, when thy king is the son of nobles, and thy princes eat in due season, for strength, and not for drunkenness!

18.web: By slothfulness the roof sinks in; and through idleness of the hands the house leaks.
18.asv: By slothfulness the roof sinketh in; and through idleness of the hands the house leaketh.

19.web: A feast is made for laughter, and wine makes the life glad; and money is the answer for all things.
19.asv: A feast is made for laughter, and wine maketh glad the life; and money answereth all things.

20.web: Don’t curse the king, no, not in your thoughts; and don’t curse the rich in your bedroom: for a bird of the sky may carry your voice, and that which has wings may tell the matter.
20.asv: Revile not the king, no, not in thy thought; and revile not the rich in thy bedchamber: for a bird of the heavens shall carry the voice, and that which hath wings shall tell the matter.
